title: Replace the dead coil element on an electric range's right front burner
instruction: The right front burner's coil element is dead. Replace it with the new one without levering the receptacle, and finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Plug-in coil ranges are still common in homes and rentals, and when one burner stops heating, the fix is to swap its coil element: a part that costs about US$50 and plugs in by hand. The makers' manuals give the method (GE): lift the unit about 1 inch above the drip pan and pull it out, then insert the terminals of the new one through the opening in the drip pan and into the receptacle and guide it into place so it rests evenly; lifting a plugged-in unit more than 1 inch can permanently damage the receptacle. The hard part is physical: a 19 cm, 0.45 kg coil has to be held level with its far edge just over the pan's lip while its two blades go 24 mm into a receptacle hidden under the deck's edge, then lowered flat.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) The cooktop of a 30-inch (76.2 cm wide) plug-in coil electric range, GE/Hotpoint style, unplugged: a white porcelain-enamel steel deck 35 mm above the table, its front edge 7.5 cm forward, running from 33 cm right to 43.2 cm left of the centre line, with the backguard (four black control knobs, all OFF, and a clock) at its back, 71 to 75 cm forward. Fixed. (2) The right front burner, centred 30 cm forward and 13 cm right: an 8-inch chrome drip pan (Range Kleen Style B, steel) in the deck's well, its lip 22.4 to 24.8 cm across and 2 mm proud of the deck, a ledge 12 mm below the deck inside the lip, the bowl 30 mm deep; a 44 mm notch in the lip toward the range's centre (left). Under the deck at the notch, the burner's receptacle (GE WB17T10006 porcelain terminal block in its screwed-down metal holder): two blade slots 4 mm wide, opening toward the well 3 to 13.5 mm below the deck surface, under the deck's edge. (3) In that pan, plugged in: the dead coil, a GE WB30M2 8-inch plug-in element (2350 W), 6 turns of 7.5 x 6.5 mm steel sheath, 19.1 cm across, on a steel Y-frame with two feet, a steel terminal bracket (25 x 16 x 16 mm) at its left edge with two steel blades 25 mm long, 2 mm thick and 13 mm apart, 0.45 kg; its sheath weathered grey-brown. It stands on its feet and bracket on the pan's ledge, its top level with the deck, blades 24 mm into the receptacle. (4) The new coil, the same part (new, black sheath), lying flat on the deck between the front burners, centred 17.5 cm forward and 4.2 cm left, terminals toward the left. (5) The left front burner, centred 30 cm forward and 25 cm left: a 6-inch chrome pan with its cold 6-inch coil plugged in. (6) The two rear burners (6-inch right, 8-inch left), centred 58.5 cm forward, cold, with their pans and coils. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Real trial: a used 30-inch GE or Hotpoint plug-in coil range, unplugged at the wall, its cooktop 35 mm above the arms' table (the range on the floor and the arms on a platform, or the cooktop assembly lifted off a range and set on blocks); one dead and one new GE WB30M2 element (a dead one: any WB30M2 with an open circuit, or a new one marked as dead).
scoring: Latched for the rest of the trial: 0.0 once either coil has fallen off the range top, or has been tilted 10 degrees or more (its far edge about 33 mm, 1.3 in, out of level) while one of its blades is 3 mm or more into the receptacle (strained). Otherwise judged at the end of the trial, on live states: 1.0: the new coil seated in the right front well (both blades 20 mm or more into the receptacle, level within 3 mm across its 19 cm, its centre within 6 mm of the well's centre), the dead coil out of that well (its centre 15 cm or more from the well's centre, blades out) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the same with an arm not back; 0.5: the dead coil out and the new coil's blades in the receptacle (3 mm or more), not seated; 0.25: the dead coil out; else 0.0. The dead coil may be set down anywhere on the range top outside the right front well. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with both coils still. In a real trial: seated means the terminal bracket's face within 5 mm of the receptacle's face, seen through the pan's notch (a close photo with a ruler), the rim level within 3 mm (a straightedge across the coil and a ruler at both ends) and the gap between the outer turn and the pan's lip even all round within 6 mm (a photo from above with a ruler). Blades in at all: the bracket within 22 mm of the receptacle's face. Strained: the video shows a plugged-in coil's far edge lifted more than 33 mm above the pan (a card marked at 33 mm stands at the well's far side). Fallen: the video shows a coil landing off the range top. The dead coil's place is checked from the end photo; the arms against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Unplug the new coil (lift its far edge about an inch, pull it straight out) and lay it back on the deck between the front burners, terminals toward the left; plug the dead coil back into the right front well, terminals through the pan's notch, and lower it flat.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz). Real sizes; coil mass 0.45 kg (computed). The range top, pans and receptacle are fixed (the pans can't be knocked out of their recesses). The receptacle's spring contacts are drawn as plain chamfered slots: the blades slide in against friction only. The coils' spiral is drawn as six concentric turns. The receptacle lever limit (10 degrees) is a design value. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
